reader.sub: Translated from the SBL Greek New Testament. Tap a verse to see why it reads as it does. Small letters mark footnotes, listed below the passage.
reader.title: Title

hint_level.L: Follows the Greek closely. Words in [brackets] are added for sense.
hint_level.B: Natural English that tracks the Greek closely. The default.
hint_level.R: Plain modern English for first-time and young readers.

hint_gender: Inclusive: “all people” where the original means everyone.
hint_christos: “Messiah”: shows it is a title meaning “anointed king”.
hint_deity_pronoun: “he”: lowercase, like the original, which has no capital letters.
“He”: capitalised, as some readers prefer out of reverence.
reader.ui.partial: Some sentences in this chapter are not yet translated; they are shown in English, in grey.
reader.ui.empty_text: Tap or click any verse to see the Greek, a word-for-word gloss, and every translation decision with its reason.
reader.ui.word_hint: Tap a Greek word for its dictionary form and grammar.
reader.ui.no_meaning: No meaning notes for this verse.
reader.ui.no_rendering: No wording notes for this level.

read.title: Read
read.heading: Books and chapters translated so far
read.dek: Each passage is translated from the SBL Greek New Testament at three levels, with the reasoning behind every sentence. English comes first; Spanish follows, and where a sentence is not yet in Spanish the reader shows the English. All are AI-assisted, and none is marked reviewed until a reviewer who reads Greek approves it.
read.step1: Choose how it reads. Literal, Balanced or Readable, and your wording settings: inclusive or traditional language, “Christ” or “Messiah”, he or He.
read.step2: Tap any verse. The Greek appears with a word-for-word gloss beside the translation.
read.step3: See every decision. What the original means, what else was considered, why this wording was chosen, and which calls are uncertain.
home.eyebrow: Free · From the Hebrew and Greek · Public domain
home.heading: The Bible, translated from Hebrew and Greek, with its reasoning shown.
home.sub: Open Word Bible is a free translation for every reader. Open any sentence to see the original words, a word-for-word gloss, and why each word was chosen. Everything is released under CC0, so anyone may use it for anything.
home.example_foot: Every verse in the reader opens like this.
home.point1_text: The translation, its notes and its data are public domain (CC0). Quote it, print it, put it in an app, or build on it without asking.
home.point2_text: Every language is translated from the Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek, never from English, using fixed, openly licensed source texts.
home.point3_text: Literal, Balanced or Readable; inclusive or traditional gender language; “Christ” or “Messiah”. Settings change wording, never meaning.
home.point4_text: Each sentence records what the original says, what we chose, what else we considered, and why. Uncertain calls are marked uncertain.
home.progress_text: The translation is AI-assisted, in English, with Spanish for some passages. Nothing is marked reviewed until named reviewers who read Hebrew or Greek approve it.
home.involve_text: Open Word Bible is built in the open. Every sentence waits for people who can check it.
home.helper1_text: Reviewers check each sentence and its decisions before it is marked reviewed.
home.helper2_text: Check that the Spanish reads naturally at each level.
home.helper3_text: The site, validator and data tools are open source (MIT).
home.helper4_text: Use the text and its reasoning records in your own app, study or project.
about.title: About
about.intro: Open Word Bible translates the Bible from its original languages into modern ones, English and Spanish first. Every sentence carries a record of the original words and the reasoning behind each translation decision.
about.licences_text: The translation, its reasoning records and the alignments are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0. The code is MIT-licensed. The source texts keep their own licences, credited below.
about.credits_language: The credits are given in English, with names and licences as their authors publish them.
articles.title: Articles
articles.heading: How the translation is made, and why it reads as it does
articles.dek: Short pieces on the method behind Open Word Bible and close readings of the passages translated so far. Like the translation, every article is a draft until a reviewer has checked it.
article.not_translated: This article is not yet translated. Here it is in English for now.
article.read_passage_text: Open it in the reader, tap any verse, and every decision behind it is there.
account.title: Account
account.signed_out_dek: Sign in to keep highlights, bookmarks and notes, and to suggest edits or ask questions about a translation. There is no password: we email you a link that signs you in.
account.privacy: Your email is used only to sign you in. Your notes and highlights are private to you.
account.sent_dek: Check your inbox at . The link signs you in once, within 20 minutes. It may take a minute to arrive; look in spam if it does not.
account.confirm_dek: One more step: finish signing in on this device. (The link works once; this step stops email scanners from using it up before you do.)
account.display_name_note: (shown to reviewers on suggestions and questions)
account.soon_text: Highlights, bookmarks and private notes on any verse, synced across your devices; then suggesting an edit or asking a question about a translation decision.
